results.reason: Issue 3 locates the problem in SA §13.2. It notes that Supplier may assign freely, to anyone including a Calder Ridge competitor, without notice, while Customer needs consent. It proposes a competitor-consent requirement and a Customer termination right. The risk explanation is thin: it touches supply continuity only through the 'leave without a source' point and never mentions confidential specs.

Issue 3 cites SA §13.3: change of control needs Supplier consent and triggers a termination right. It explains that this gives Norvane hold-up leverage over any sale, merger or financing and recommends deletion or a competitor-only fallback. The memo treats a sale as hypothetical and asks the client whether one is planned, but the substance is covered.
Issue 4 identifies the OF §2.2 three-year auto-renewal with 30-day notice and explains the lock-in risk. It recommends no auto-renewal, or one-year renewals with 90-day notice.
Issue 2 flags the uncapped Customer indemnity under §9.3 against Supplier's capped liability. It recommends deleting §9.3 and replacing it with a mutual carve-out.
The memo correctly states the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months (§9.1), the three-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026, and Delaware law and forum.
The memo states the SA > OF > Spec precedence and applies it to the renewal conflict, invoicing timing and the inspection window.
Issues are tiered, with a 'Raise First' Tier 1. Indemnity/cap (Issue 2) and change of control (Issue 3) are both in Tier 1, and a call sequence is suggested.
Each issue sets out Where, Problem/Why it matters and Fix, with proposed language. A separate 'Points Needing Client Input' section appears at the end.

The memo treats the Specifications Schedule as a source of significant issues: Issue 1 (part mismatch, circular definition) and Issue 13 (spec gaps). It also cites UCC § 2-316 / 6 Del. C. § 2-316, which is outside authority not found in the documents.
